 18 Nov 2026 Every word of Renée's pre-Lyon press conference
 Arsenal Media 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 Renée Slegers was back in front of the media for her pre-Lyon press conference at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Wednesday.
 Our head coach sat down to look ahead to Thursday's UEFA Women's Champions League clash at Meadow Park.
 Here's everything she had to say on the following subjects...
 on what we can take from the Barcelona and London City games to prepare for Lyon: 
They are three different teams, so Barcelona work with very close relationships, close connections on the pitch, London City was a little different in that sense, but there were similarities. What they do similarly is very high and aggressive pressure, jump pressure. Lyon are a very athletic team as well, they have a lot of fast players, so we’ll have to manage that really well and defend that really well, and make sure that we’re in good areas on the pitch and have numbers around the ball. It will be a different game, it’s also a different pitch. So what we’ll do to turn that into a win is do our very best to put a good plan together that the players are going to execute. This game is different in that sense, I think we’ll have to manage their speed in this game and look at our chances as well. 
 on if we will prioritise not conceding or scoring goals against Lyon: 
It goes hand-in-hand, we played against Barcelona and I think at that point they had scored 19 as well and conceded two, so very similar scenario in that sense, but two different types of teams. What we’ll have to do is we want to play our game, the last two games we’ve spent less time on the ball. Our ambition is to spend more time on the ball tomorrow, that helps us defend as well because if you’re on the ball, you’re automatically not defending, so that’s important for us tomorrow. But also a huge respect for the team they are, the qualities that they possess and the game that they’re going to bring to us. We’ve played against them a lot lately in the last two years, so a huge respect for what they’ve achieved so far, and we’ll look forward to the game tomorrow. 
 on if we’ve been working on set-pieces ahead of a game against a physical side: 
Yes, we're working on our set-pieces. We know it's an important area for us. We create a lot of corners. If I go into corners specifically, it's something we want to do better. Also, when it doesn't happen in open play, there's always the set-piece. That's something we're working on definitely for tomorrow. It's of course the defending set-pieces as well, with the threat that they have, which is important in the game plan. We'll have to look at what we can create against them because we won't be taller than Wendie Renard, so we'll have to find other solutions and ideas.
 on if Sunday’s match was an exciting advert for women’s football: 
Very good game of football. Especially the first half, I think maybe you saw some fatigue coming into the second half, end of the second half, but the first half was fantastic football and we scored a great goal early in the game. We are front-footed, intense, and find solutions fast in moments. So, no, really good football, which is great. I think many people talk about it, the WSL being the best league potentially in the world right now. I think if you look at that game, for example, it was a really good game of football, which is important. That's the product that we want to deliver, but for us, of course, with the draws that we've had, we needed and wanted to convert that into three points, which we didn't do on Sunday.
 on if we’re expecting an open, unpredictable match against Lyon: 
We have to accept that it's open at times with the way they play, but our preference is that it's not too open. We want to control it, we want to control spaces, we want to control the game a little bit better, spend time on the ball, but then we also know that when there are spaces given and opportunities, we are good when things go fast, so we'll have to be really good dictating tempo and choosing what to do when in the game.
 on what it’s like to have Maanum back: 
Yeah, great. We just spoke about the freedom on the pitch, and I'm happy you feel that way. I think one of Frida's qualities as well is positional intelligence and discipline as well, so that balance and those two things that Frida can bring both to the game is fantastic and helps the team, makes other players better around her. And now, also at the end of two chances, it's really good to have Frida back and it means a lot to us. Two 90s after a while out, so really good physically as well, so now really happy to have Frida back.
 on how the atmosphere at Meadow Park helps the team: 
I think the closeness, the closeness to the people. You feel that, you feel the energy in the stands. You can almost hear what they say and you feel that connection even more. I like that about playing at Meadow Park. The challenge is that it's all very open and close to the opposition, so for us to find a code language down the sideline, maybe. No, we love going there and it's a special ground for Arsenal Women. That's where it all started, so it is special that we're still playing there. Of course, in combination with the Emirates, which really feels like our home as well.
